question.problem: Determine the equation of the level curve that passes through the point $P(0,1)$ for the function $f(x,y)=\frac{3x+2}{1-3y}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the value of the function at $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0,1) & =\frac{3(0)+2}{1-3(1)} \\  & =\frac{0+2}{1-3} \\  & =\frac{2}{(-2)} \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the level curve that passes through $P(0,1)$ is the $-1$-level curve.

Recall that the level curves for the function $f(x,y)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=-1.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =c \\ \frac{3x+2}{1-3y} & =-1 \\ 3x+2 & =-(1-3y) \\ 3x+2 & =3y-1 \\ 3y & =3x+3 \\ y & =x+1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level curve that passes through $P(0,1)$ is the line $y=x+1.$
